_comment: The ingest slice contract: the raw Claude Code transcript a PreCompact or SessionEnd hook reads, the wire slice it posts to the MCP `ingest` tool, and the flattened slice the server hands extraction. tests/plugin/test_ingest_hook.py writes `transcript` out as JSON Lines, runs the real hooks/ingest.sh and asserts the posted `slice` argument equals `wire`. tests/cli/test_ingest.py asserts the CLI's slicer turns `transcript` into `wire`. The server's tests read `wire`, `wire_refusals` and `slice` from their own copy of this file, so a change here needs the same change there.
_slice_comment: Exactly three keys per line: uuid, role and content. `cwd` is a local filesystem path that can carry a username or a project name off the machine, and `sessionId`, `parentUuid` and `version` are machine-local metadata, so none of them is sent. `content` is flattened to a string: text blocks joined, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks dropped, because tool results are file contents, environment dumps and command output, which is where secrets live.
_uuid_comment: The uuids are the transcript's own. The server cites one per extracted fact and deduplicates on it, so a slice without uuids cannot deduplicate. Changing a uuid or a body here changes a dedupe key on the server.
_transcript_comment: One Claude Code transcript record per entry, carrying the fields the real file carries. The rows exercise every narrowing the hook owes: `cwd`/`sessionId`/`parentUuid`/`version` are present and must not survive; content arrives both as a bare string and as a block array; an assistant row pairs text with a `thinking` block and a `tool_use` block and only the text survives; a `type: user` row whose whole content is a `tool_result` block leaves no message; and a row with no `uuid` leaves no message, because a candidate drawn from it could cite nothing. Those last two rows are why `wire` is shorter than `transcript`.

slice.content: Before we touch the retrieval handler, remind me what a recall actually reads today.
Retrieval reads the main branch plus the caller's own branch, and rows drawn from the caller's own branch come back marked unreviewed. That is settled — it is what recall does now, not a proposal.
Right. And we decided agents write only to their own branch at agents/<client-id>/<user> — an agent never opens a proposal itself any more. Treat that as the rule from here on.
Understood. Let me read the promotion service before I say anything about how the branch gets promoted.
One more thing to write down: a repository under automatic promotion holds at most one open proposal per branch, and a scheduled sweep rolls newly written facts into it. Don't open a second one.
Noted. I will keep the roll-into-the-existing-proposal shape and leave the scheduler to open at most one.
